recommendations.regimenLabel: IV corticosteroids + VTE prophylaxis (acute severe UC); oral steroids for Crohn's flare
steps: EXCLUDE infective colitis (stool culture + C. difficile toxin) before/with immunosuppression.
Acute severe UC: admit, IV corticosteroids, VTE prophylaxis, monitor (Truelove-Witts / day-3 response).
Steroid-refractory severe UC: rescue ciclosporin or infliximab; early surgical review (colectomy).
Crohn's flare: corticosteroids to induce remission; optimise/escalate maintenance (immunomodulator/biologic).
Avoid antimotility agents in severe colitis (toxic megacolon risk); nutrition support.

drugRefs.dose: 100 mg IV four times daily (or methylprednisolone 60 mg/day)
drugRefs.why: First-line to induce remission in acute severe UC; assess response at day 3 (stool frequency/CRP) to decide on rescue therapy.

drugRefs.dose: 40 mg PO once daily, then taper
drugRefs.why: Induces remission in a Crohn's or moderate UC flare; tapered course, not for maintenance.
Active IBD is strongly prothrombotic; prophylactic LMWH is recommended in hospitalised flares despite rectal bleeding.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Inflammatory Bowel Disease
ECCO Guidelines on Ulcerative Colitis and Crohn's Disease (Medical Management)
BSG Consensus Guidelines on the Management of IBD in Adults

recommendations.regimenLabel: Rescue therapy for steroid-refractory acute severe UC

drugRefs.dose: 2 mg/kg/day IV infusion (adjust to trough levels)
drugRefs.why: Rescue option in steroid-refractory acute severe UC to avoid/bridge to colectomy; requires level and renal monitoring.
Alternative rescue for steroid-refractory acute severe UC; screen for TB/hepatitis B before use.

decision.label: Exclude infection; IV steroids + VTE prophylaxis if severe

confirm: Bloody diarrhoea, urgency, abdominal pain ± systemic features in known/new IBD; raised CRP/faecal calprotectin; exclude infection (incl. C. difficile).
